raw_text: Worker began maintenance on electrical equipment without verifying isolation. The equipment remained energized during the task. A supervisor later noted the lockout procedure was not followed.
Worker was struck by drill pipe during equipment operation after entering the line of fire zone. No exclusion zone had been established. The worker was fatally injured on impact.

Worker was exposed to flying fragments after the grinder guard was removed to access a tight area. No injury occurred but fragments struck the face shield. Guard had been removed without authorization.

A hydrocarbon release occurred after process isolation was not adequately verified before maintenance commenced. Residual pressure remained in the line. A small fire resulted but was quickly suppressed.

Worker entered a confined space without documented atmospheric testing for oxygen deficiency or toxic gas. No gas detector was available at the entry point. Worker was hospitalized for exposure symptoms.
Inspector was working at 12 metres height without a fall arrest harness. The safety harness was available in the toolbox but not worn. Wind conditions were moderate. No injury occurred.
Crane operator lifted a suspended load over a work area where another worker was present. The load slipped from rigging due to sling failure. The worker below was fatally struck.
Maintenance technician began work on compressor without confirming the energy isolation permit. Residual stored pressure was released when a fitting was removed. Worker sustained burns to forearm.
Hot work was conducted within 10 metres of a fuel storage tank without a hot work permit. No gas monitoring was in place. Sparks reached the bund but no ignition occurred.
Heavy vehicle driver reversed without a spotter in a restricted area. A worker on foot was struck and received a broken leg. Pedestrian exclusion zones were not enforced in this area.
Worker was inside an unshored excavation approximately 2.1 metres deep when a wall collapse occurred. No shoring or benching was in place. The worker was buried and fatally injured.
Electrician received a shock while working on a live panel that was believed to be de-energised. Isolation was verified at the wrong isolation point. Burns to hands resulted.

Gas detector alarm was acknowledged but not investigated. A flammable gas cloud subsequently ignited causing a flash fire. Two workers received burns. The alarm had sounded three times in the previous hour.
Welder was conducting hot work adjacent to a storage rack containing aerosol cans. No hot work permit had been issued. A supervisor stopped the work before ignition occurred.
Worker was exposed to sudden well pressure surge during maintenance on a valve without a pressure isolation being in place. The valve ejected and the worker was struck. Fatality resulted.
Maintenance worker was on a flat roof without edge protection or fall arrest equipment. Work involved replacing a HVAC unit near the roof edge. No fall prevention controls were implemented.
Incorrect chemical was loaded into a reaction vessel because labelling was inadequate. An exothermic reaction resulted. Emergency shutdown activated. No injuries but significant equipment damage.
Forklift operator struck a pedestrian in a shared access zone. No pedestrian segregation barriers were in place. The pedestrian sustained a fracture. Speed limits were not enforced.
Worker was maintaining a press and reached into the machine while the power was connected. No lockout was in place. The press cycled and the worker sustained fatal crush injuries.
Scaffolding was erected by workers who were not certified scaffold erectors. Incomplete board coverage on the 3rd lift. A worker stepped through a gap and fell approximately 3 metres. Hospitalized.

Corrosion inspection revealed wall thinning below minimum acceptable thickness on a high-pressure gas pipeline section. No reduction in operating pressure had been requested. Potential catastrophic rupture identified.
Two workers entered a sewer-type confined space to retrieve a dropped tool. Neither atmospheric testing nor a permit was obtained. Both workers were overcome by hydrogen sulphide. Both hospitalized.
Worker was guiding a suspended load by hand when the crane moved unexpectedly. The load swung and struck the worker causing a fractured pelvis. No tag line was in use.
Contractor electrician accessed a high-voltage switchroom without site-specific induction and without being accompanied. No injury but contractor was found in a restricted energised area without PPE.
Isolation valve was closed but no blind or spade was inserted before breaking a flange on a hydrocarbon line. The valve passed and hydrocarbon liquid sprayed the worker causing chemical burns.

Driller entered the drill floor while pipe was in motion without communicating with the drawworks operator. A near miss with rotating pipe resulted. No personnel alarm or communication protocol followed.

Worker was cleaning inside a storage tank without an inert atmosphere confirmation or continuous monitoring. Hydrocarbon vapour accumulated. Ignition source from a torch caused an explosion. Fatal outcome.

Generator was running when a technician opened the access panel to investigate an alarm. No isolation was performed. The technician received an electric shock and burns. Burns required hospitalisation.

Hot work permit was issued but gas monitoring was stopped after one hour. Work continued for two additional hours without continuous monitoring. Combustible gas accumulation was found on post-work survey.

Crane lift plan had not been prepared for a non-routine heavy lift. The load exceeded the crane's rated capacity at the operating radius by 12%. The crane tipped but the load was retained. No injuries.
Driver of a heavy transport vehicle fell asleep at the wheel on a site access road. Vehicle left the road and struck earthworks. The driver was fatally injured.
Worker fell from a 4-metre-high stepladder that was not footed or secured. The ladder slipped while the worker was reaching laterally. The worker sustained a fractured wrist.

Instrument technician bypassed a critical safety instrumented system for maintenance without management of change approval. The bypass remained in place for 48 hours. A process exceedance occurred during this period.

Inspector entered a manhole after atmospheric testing showed acceptable oxygen but did not test for H2S. H2S was subsequently detected by a personal monitor at dangerous levels. Inspector evacuated safely.
Electrician was performing switching operations without a second person present as required by procedure. An arc flash occurred due to equipment fault. The electrician suffered fatal burns.

Fuel tanker driver left the tanker unattended while fuelling a piece of equipment. Overfill occurred and fuel spilled onto hot exhaust. A small fire resulted. No injuries but significant environmental impact.

During maintenance on a reciprocating compressor the technician failed to depressurise the system before removing a valve cover. The cover ejected under pressure and struck the technician in the face causing eye injury.

Hot work was conducted above a drain connected to a hydrocarbon system. Molten metal droplets fell into the drain and caused a small hydrocarbon fire in the drain. Fire was extinguished with extinguisher.
Worker was transferring corrosive acid without acid-resistant PPE. Pump seal failed and acid sprayed the worker over a large body surface area. Worker received fatal chemical burns.
Scaffold board was placed unsupported with overhang exceeding four times board thickness. A worker stepped onto the overhang and the board flipped. Worker grabbed a handrail and was not injured.
Observed worker operating valve without required PPE (gloves, safety glasses). H2S gas present in the area. Toolbox talk conducted but worker not aware of specific hazards.
BOP valve operated without confirming well pressure status. No well control permit in place. Well was in a live state. Pressure spike occurred but well was regained without blowout.

Maintenance person observed bypassing interlocks on pump protection system to prevent spurious shutdown. Bypass placed without authorisation or management of change. High vibration subsequently detected.

Chemical injection pump seal failed and methanol sprayed the maintenance technician. Technician was not wearing face shield or acid/chemical resistant suit as required by chemical handling procedure. First aid treatment required.

Inspector identified that the flare knockout drum high-level shutdown had been disabled for more than one week without a bypass permit or management of change. Multiple near-miss conditions present during this period.
Hot work observed being conducted within the restricted zone around the diesel bund without a hot work permit and without fire watch. Contractor crew performing welding repairs.

Compressor overpressure event occurred due to pressure relief valve being gagged (held closed with wire) by maintenance to stop spurious lifting. Relief valve was not restored before restart. Overpressure reached 142% design pressure.
Observed smoking in a non-designated area adjacent to fuel storage facility. Fire risk in proximity to fuel. Area is classified as restricted smoking zone.

Pipeline patrol found third party excavation activity occurring within the pipeline corridor without prior notification to OIL. Excavation machinery operating within 2 metres of live pipeline. Pipeline undamaged but excavation immediately stopped.

Electrician received an electric shock while testing a circuit that had been thought to be de-energised. Isolation had been applied at the wrong distribution board. Worker hospitalized with hand burns.
